item.content:encoded:
Forced migration and refugee movements remain among the most pressing humanitarian, political, and social challenges of the 21st century. Armed conflicts, climate change, political instability, persecution, and human rights violations continue to force millions of people from their homes every year. At the same time, many governments are adopting increasingly restrictive migration policies, making refugee protection more complex than ever before.

To address these global challenges through education and evidence-based learning, the Refugee Studies Centre (RSC) at the University of Oxford is offering its internationally acclaimed International Online School in Forced Migration during the 2026–2027 academic year. This prestigious programme brings together participants from across the globe to deepen their understanding of forced migration through expert-led teaching, academic discussions, networking, and collaborative learning.

Recognized internationally as one of the leading educational programmes in the field of forced migration, the International Online School provides an opportunity for professionals, researchers, students, and policy-makers to engage with world-renowned scholars while balancing their professional commitments through an accessible online learning format.

Programme Dates

The Refugee Studies Centre will host the International Online School twice during the 2026–2027 academic year:

  • 7–11 December 2026
  • 21–25 June 2027

This expanded schedule responds to increasing global demand while ensuring that participants from different regions have greater flexibility to attend.

About the Refugee Studies Centre

The Refugee Studies Centre (RSC), part of the Oxford Department of International Development at the University of Oxford, is internationally recognized for its research, teaching, and policy engagement on forced migration and refugee issues.

For decades, the Centre has contributed significantly to advancing scholarship, informing humanitarian practice, and shaping migration policy across the world. Its International School reflects this long-standing commitment to academic excellence, interdisciplinary research, and practical engagement.

Why Forced Migration Studies Matter Today

The global displacement crisis continues to evolve rapidly.

Today’s forced migration landscape includes:

  • Refugees fleeing armed conflicts
  • Internally displaced persons (IDPs)
  • Asylum seekers
  • Stateless populations
  • Climate-induced displacement
  • Cross-border humanitarian emergencies
  • Protracted refugee situations
  • Urban displacement

As humanitarian needs continue to rise, professionals working in government agencies, international organizations, NGOs, research institutions, and academia require deeper analytical skills and evidence-based understanding to design effective responses.

The International Online School provides participants with the opportunity to critically examine these complex issues from multiple academic and professional perspectives.

What Makes the International Online School Unique?

Unlike many short online courses, the International Online School emphasizes rigorous scholarship while remaining highly accessible to busy professionals.

The programme combines:

  • Academic excellence
  • Practical relevance
  • Global perspectives
  • Interactive learning
  • International networking
  • Evidence-based teaching

Rather than offering simplified overviews, the course encourages participants to critically engage with complex migration issues using research-informed approaches.

Flexible Online Learning Structure

The programme is specifically designed for participants who may already be working full-time.

Learning takes place in two stages.

Before the Live School

Participants receive access to:

  • Pre-recorded lectures
  • Curated readings
  • Learning exercises
  • Preparatory materials

These resources allow participants to build foundational knowledge before the interactive sessions begin.

During the Live School

Participants then join an intensive week featuring:

  • Live seminars
  • Interactive discussions
  • Expert lectures
  • Academic debates
  • Collaborative learning sessions
  • Networking opportunities
  • Professional exchanges

This blended approach ensures that participants maximize their learning experience while engaging directly with internationally recognized experts.

Academic Standards

The International Online School reflects the Refugee Studies Centre’s commitment to:

  • Rigorous academic research
  • Evidence-based teaching
  • Inclusive learning
  • Critical thinking
  • Interdisciplinary scholarship
  • High pedagogical standards

Participants are encouraged not only to gain knowledge but also to question assumptions, evaluate evidence, and develop more sophisticated understandings of forced migration.

Curriculum Focus

The programme explores forced migration through multiple disciplinary perspectives rather than relying on a single framework.

Participants can expect discussions related to:

  • Refugee protection
  • Forced displacement
  • Humanitarian responses
  • Migration governance
  • International law
  • Human rights
  • Historical perspectives
  • Anthropological approaches
  • Psychosocial dimensions of displacement
  • Public policy
  • Research methodologies
  • Contemporary global migration challenges

The curriculum encourages participants to understand forced migration as a multidimensional issue requiring interdisciplinary solutions.

Networking Opportunities

One of the most valuable aspects of the programme is the opportunity to connect with participants from around the world.

Networking activities allow participants to:

  • Exchange professional experiences
  • Build international collaborations
  • Share regional perspectives
  • Learn from practitioners across sectors
  • Expand global professional networks
  • Develop lasting academic and professional relationships

Participants engage with colleagues representing diverse institutions, countries, and disciplines.

Learning from Leading Experts

The programme is led by internationally recognized scholars and practitioners specializing in forced migration.

Participants benefit from:

  • Expert instruction
  • Current research
  • Practical case studies
  • Evidence-based discussions
  • Academic mentorship
  • Global perspectives

This ensures that learning reflects both cutting-edge research and real-world humanitarian practice.

Participant Testimonials

Feedback from previous participants highlights the programme’s impact.

Participants have described the International Online School as:

  • A unique opportunity to learn from world-leading scholars and practitioners.
  • An intellectually rigorous yet welcoming learning environment.
  • A programme that encourages thinking beyond daily professional responsibilities.
  • A transformative educational experience that challenges assumptions and promotes critical thinking.
  • An opportunity to gain a richer understanding of migration through multiple disciplinary perspectives.
  • A course that distinguishes rigorous scholarship from advocacy by emphasizing reflection and evidence.
  • A platform for meaningful knowledge exchange among professionals from different regions and backgrounds.

These testimonials demonstrate the programme’s reputation for combining academic excellence with practical relevance.

Benefits of Participating

Participants in the International Online School can expect to gain:

  • Advanced knowledge of forced migration
  • Exposure to global research and evidence
  • Interdisciplinary understanding
  • Practical analytical skills
  • Access to internationally recognized experts
  • Opportunities for professional networking
  • Global peer learning
  • Enhanced policy and research perspectives
  • Stronger professional capacity in migration-related fields

Who Should Apply?

The programme is ideal for:

  • Refugee protection professionals
  • Humanitarian practitioners
  • NGO staff
  • Government officials
  • Policy-makers
  • Researchers
  • University lecturers
  • Graduate students
  • International development professionals
  • Human rights advocates
  • Migration specialists
  • Staff of international organizations
  • Individuals seeking to build expertise in forced migration

Visit HERE to learn more about the Oxford University International Online School in Forced Migration 2026–2027

Programme Delivery

The International Online School is delivered entirely online, making participation possible from anywhere in the world.

The learning model combines:

  • Self-paced preparation
  • Scheduled live sessions
  • Interactive seminars
  • Collaborative discussions
  • Networking events

This structure allows participants to engage deeply while maintaining flexibility.

Why Choose Oxford’s International Online School?

The programme stands out because of its:

  • Global reputation
  • University of Oxford academic excellence
  • Evidence-based curriculum
  • International faculty
  • Interactive online format
  • Interdisciplinary approach
  • Diverse participant community
  • Professional networking opportunities
  • Practical relevance for humanitarian and policy work

It remains one of the most respected online programmes available in the field of forced migration.

How to Apply

Interested applicants should visit the Refugee Studies Centre’s International Online School webpage to:

  • Review the full programme overview.
  • Explore the curriculum for 2026–2027.
  • Check fees and entry requirements.
  • Read the frequently asked questions.
  • Complete the online application process.

Since no application deadline has been announced in the available information, prospective participants are encouraged to apply as early as possible to secure a place in their preferred programme session.

APPLY HERE

Conclusion

The University of Oxford’s International Online School in Forced Migration offers an outstanding opportunity for professionals, researchers, students, and policy-makers seeking to strengthen their expertise in one of the world’s most significant humanitarian and policy challenges. Through rigorous academic teaching, expert-led discussions, interdisciplinary learning, and global networking, participants gain valuable knowledge and practical insights that can directly enhance their work in refugee protection, migration governance, humanitarian response, and international development.

With two programme sessions scheduled during the 2026–2027 academic year and a flexible online format, the International Online School provides accessible, world-class education for participants from every region of the globe. Whether you are looking to advance your career, strengthen your research, or deepen your understanding of forced migration, this internationally recognized programme represents an exceptional opportunity to learn from some of the world’s leading experts in the field.

item.content:encoded:
Applications are now open for the Transfyr AI Fellowship 2026–2027, a prestigious one-year, fully funded research fellowship designed for exceptional graduate students, recent PhD graduates, and postdoctoral researchers who are passionate about advancing frontier machine learning research with real-world scientific impact.

The fellowship offers an outstanding opportunity to work alongside leading experts in artificial intelligence, biology, robotics, and scientific research while tackling some of the most challenging problems in machine learning and scientific automation.

Successful fellows will receive $125,000 in annual compensation, comprehensive benefits, access to cutting-edge computational resources, and the opportunity to contribute to groundbreaking research that aims to transform how scientific work is understood, evaluated, and reproduced.

Based primarily in the Boston/Cambridge area, the fellowship welcomes applications from talented researchers around the world and provides visa support for selected international fellows.

About the Transfyr AI Fellowship

The Transfyr AI Fellowship was established to address one of the biggest challenges facing modern science—the absence of a comprehensive observability layer that captures how scientific work actually happens.

Scientific discovery often involves much more than published papers or laboratory protocols. It includes failed experiments, operator expertise, contextual decision-making, noisy instruments, repeated attempts, and numerous tacit processes that are rarely documented.

Transfyr is building what it describes as the world’s largest multimodal dataset of scientific execution, allowing artificial intelligence systems to understand science as it is performed in real-world laboratory environments rather than relying solely on polished publications and benchmark datasets.

The fellowship provides participants with the opportunity to work directly on these frontier challenges.

Fellowship Overview

The programme is a full-time research fellowship lasting 12 months.

Selected fellows will:

  • Lead an independent research project.
  • Work with real multimodal scientific datasets.
  • Collaborate closely with scientists, engineers, operators, and AI researchers.
  • Build prototypes and novel machine learning systems.
  • Design new evaluation frameworks.
  • Produce publishable research or demonstration-quality technical outputs.

The fellowship is intended for individuals who are interested in pushing the boundaries of machine learning while solving practical scientific problems.

Research Areas

Fellows will contribute to one or more frontier AI research challenges.

1. Multimodal Reasoning

Researchers will develop AI models capable of integrating multiple sources of scientific information.

Research topics include:

  • Video understanding
  • Audio analysis
  • Laboratory protocol interpretation
  • Instrument data
  • Temporal reasoning
  • Human activity understanding
  • Cross-modal grounding

2. Conflicting Evidence

Scientific environments frequently contain inconsistent observations.

Projects include:

  • Uncertainty estimation
  • Model calibration
  • Evidence attribution
  • Contradiction-aware reasoning

3. Long-Context Scientific Memory

Scientific workflows often extend across days, weeks, or months.

Researchers will investigate:

  • Long-term memory systems
  • Retrieval over laboratory histories
  • State tracking
  • Failure memory
  • Process compression

4. Real-World AI Evaluation

Rather than relying on traditional AI benchmarks, fellows will design evaluation systems measuring real scientific performance.

Areas include:

  • Benchmark design
  • Laboratory evaluation
  • Process-level metrics
  • Automated execution assessment

5. Tacit Scientific Expertise

Many laboratory skills cannot easily be written into protocols.

Researchers will explore:

  • Expert decision-making
  • Human expertise representation
  • Human-in-the-loop AI
  • Skill modeling
  • Expert-versus-novice comparisons

6. Physical-World AI

This research area bridges robotics and artificial intelligence.

Projects include:

  • Robotics
  • Embodied AI
  • Demonstration learning
  • Policy evaluation
  • Transfer learning

7. Biosecurity and Bio-Risk Observability

Fellows may develop AI systems capable of improving laboratory biosecurity through:

  • Workflow monitoring
  • Capability assessment
  • Autonomous vulnerability detection
  • Safety-critical containment systems

8. Scientific Execution Ontology

Researchers will build structured representations of experimental workflows including:

  • Protocol metadata
  • Laboratory preparation
  • Concentrations
  • Solubility
  • Plate setup
  • Experimental context
  • Biological variability

What Fellows Will Do

Throughout the fellowship, participants will:

  • Define an original research question.
  • Develop machine learning prototypes.
  • Analyze multimodal scientific execution data.
  • Design evaluation methodologies.
  • Produce publishable research.
  • Build technical demonstrations.
  • Develop datasets and benchmarks.

Outstanding work may be incorporated into real-world scientific products.

Mentorship and Research Environment

One of the strongest aspects of the fellowship is direct mentorship.

Fellows will work closely with:

  • Transfyr founders
  • Machine learning engineers
  • AI researchers
  • Biologists
  • Robotics experts
  • Scientific operators
  • Applied R&D specialists

This interdisciplinary environment provides exceptional opportunities for learning and collaboration.

Compensation and Benefits

Selected fellows receive an attractive financial package that includes:

Annual Compensation

  • $125,000

Additional Benefits

  • Employee benefits
  • Access to GPUs
  • Compute resources
  • Scientific datasets
  • Research support
  • Technical infrastructure

Applicants are encouraged to specify the computational resources required for their proposed research.

Fellowship Location

The programme is designed primarily for full-time, in-person participation in:

Boston/Cambridge, Massachusetts, USA

Remote participation may be approved only in exceptional circumstances where both the research project and applicant make remote collaboration feasible.

Visa Support

International researchers are encouraged to apply.

Visa sponsorship will be provided to selected fellows requiring authorization to work in the United States.

Research Outputs

Participants are expected to produce meaningful research outputs, including:

  • Journal publications
  • Technical reports
  • Benchmarks
  • Datasets
  • Software prototypes
  • Research demonstrations

While fellows are encouraged to publish their work, Transfyr retains ownership of fellowship work products, with publication subject to confidentiality and intellectual property review.

Who Should Apply?

The programme seeks outstanding researchers with strong technical backgrounds and intellectual curiosity.

Ideal applicants include:

  • Current graduate students
  • Recent PhD graduates
  • Postdoctoral researchers

Relevant academic disciplines include:

  • Machine Learning
  • Artificial Intelligence
  • Computer Science
  • Computational Biology
  • Robotics
  • Human-Computer Interaction
  • Statistics
  • Related computational disciplines

Applicants should demonstrate:

  • Strong machine learning expertise
  • Excellent research ability
  • Creativity
  • Curiosity
  • Comfort working on ambiguous research challenges

Programme Timeline

Applications are reviewed on a rolling basis.

Rolling Review

Applications are evaluated as they are received.

Full Consideration Deadline

Applicants are encouraged to submit by:

15 August 2026

Decision Timeline

Selection decisions will be made on a rolling basis through:

Late August 2026

Fellowship Start Date

Selected fellows are expected to begin around:

September 2026

Application Requirements

The application process has been intentionally designed to be concise.

Applicants must submit:

  • A one-page application.
  • Description of the research project they wish to pursue.
  • Required computational resources.
  • Links showcasing previous work.

Finalists will later be asked to provide academic references.

                                                                 APPLY HERE

For More Information

Interested applicants can learn more about the fellowship and explore the available research problems HERE

For enquiries regarding the fellowship or application process, applicants may contact:

Email: ai_fellowship@transfyr.ai

Applicants are encouraged to submit their applications as early as possible because reviews are conducted on a rolling basis and early submissions receive the greatest consideration.

Conclusion

The Transfyr AI Fellowship 2026–2027 represents an exceptional opportunity for graduate students, recent PhD graduates, and postdoctoral researchers who aspire to work at the intersection of artificial intelligence and scientific discovery. Offering a competitive annual compensation of $125,000, world-class mentorship, access to advanced computational resources, and the opportunity to contribute to pioneering research with real-world scientific applications, the fellowship provides an ideal environment for ambitious researchers to make meaningful contributions to frontier machine learning. Interested applicants from around the world are encouraged to submit their applications by 15 August 2026 for full consideration and take the next step toward shaping the future of AI-driven scientific research.
